historical_anchors.25th_Dragoons_equipment: M3 Lee/Grant-class 30-ton medium tanks with 75mm hull gun + 37mm turret gun
movement: British official history: 25th Dragoons secretly disembarked by night near Ukhia on 1943-12-02.
254th Indian Tank Brigade history: 25th Dragoons + engineer troop + motor infantry company detached to XV Corps effective 1943-12-05.
Personal/regimental evidence places the regiment moving through the Chittagong-Arakan route in late 1943.
historical_anchors.support: Engineer support included route/bridge preparation; historical employment later demonstrated effective jungle bunker-busting.

Japanese_state: Chittagong falls centered late 1943-12-14 in current settlement
branch_collision.consequence: Historical Ukhia landing route is unavailable. British command must reroute, delay, or commit the incoming regiment defensively through Chittagong/Feni-side LOC.
branch_collision.mandatory: 25th Dragoons cannot be omitted merely because the branch offensive is earlier; its already-scheduled transfer is an independent Allied reinforcement clock.

combat_implications: Japanese 55th Division has no centered tank regiment, so this is mainly Allied medium tanks versus Japanese infantry AT guns, artillery, mines, engineers and air attack.
M3 Lee/Grant 75mm HE materially strengthens British counterattack and bunker/field-position destruction where roads/bridges permit.
30-ton weight, high silhouette, limited hull-gun traverse, bridges, paddy/mud and Japanese air/artillery prevent unrestricted maneuver.
Japanese 47mm-class AT fire can be dangerous from flank/close-range geometry but is not a reliable frontal solution; 37mm-class weapons are much less satisfactory.
British use can delay or locally reverse Japanese road-axis advances even without changing the whole campaign.
